subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define this anti-drift behavior as a core execution enforcement contract, and what durable state, artifact, timer, feature-flag, and telemetry semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested fix defines cross-cutting runtime policy and persistent state behavior that automation cannot safely choose from the issue text alone.

options.title: Design Core Guard Contract
options.body: Define a single additive guard contract for artifact-backed progress, blocker escalation, durable state, post-green follow-through, and telemetry before assigning implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Atomic Lifecycle Work
options.body: Treat this as acceptance criteria for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/17213 so begin, execution evidence, commit or abort, and blocker semantics share one lifecycle contract.

options.title: Defer To Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep current liveness, no-fake-progress, poll backoff, and tool-loop safeguards while asking for a live trace before adding new enforcement state.

recommendation.title: Design Core Guard Contract
recommendation.body: Define a single additive guard contract for artifact-backed progress, blocker escalation, durable state, post-green follow-through, and telemetry before assigning implementation.
